{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Twenty-six years ago, President Reagan's Task Force on Victims of Crime called the neglect of crime victims a \"national disgrace\" and proposed a constitutional amendment to secure their formal rights.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Today, the neglect of crime victims persists in courtrooms across the nation.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Innocent victims—battered women, abused children, the loved ones of the murdered—still may not be told when their case is being heard.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Innocent victims can be excluded from the courtroom even when the defendant and his friends may be present.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Innocent victims have no right to a speedy trial.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A judge or parole board has no obligation to consider the personal safety of innocent victims in making release decisions.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The innocent have far fewer rights than the accused.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Support for Congress to send to the states for ratification a constitutional amendment to protect the rights of crime victims.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Crime victims should be assured of access to legal and social services.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Crime Victims Fund established under President Reagan should be used solely for providing access to legal and social services.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
